reasoning: The defect is real and precisely characterized. aux_query_1() (line 124-127) runs a SELECT via duckdb_query with a non-null out_result_p, populating an out_result buffer owned by the caller. Two consumers — test_query (132-137) and test_duckdb_column_count_and_duckdb_row_count (153-160) — call aux_close_db(), which only calls duckdb_disconnect + duckdb_close (lines 67-69), and never call duckdb_destroy_result. The DuckDB C API binding (ducklib.py:774-777) separately wraps duckdb_destroy_result, which is the only way to reclaim the memory DuckDB allocates for a result's internal data; duckdb_close/duckdb_disconnect do not free it. The consistent teardown pattern in sibling tests confirms the omission is an oversight: test_duckdb_destroy_result (line 168), test_column_name (line 921), test_result_return_type (line 979), test_column_type (line 930), test_column_logical_type (line 942), test_rows_changed (line 959), test_result_error_type_on_success (line 969), and all prepared-statement consumers all call duckdb_destroy_result before aux_close_db. Severity medium is appropriate: the leak is real (not OS-reclaimed until pytest process exit), the affected tests are inconsistent with the established teardown discipline in the rest of the suite, and their failure to destroy the result means a missing-destroy regression in those code paths would pass silently.
